text: In the NOAA NCEI marine microplastics database, by what factor did the median ocean-water concentration (pieces/m3) change from the 2000-2004 samples to the 2020-2024 samples? Does that show microplastic in the ocean rose by that factor?
rule: no study sampled in both periods, so the ratio compares different studies, places and methods

text: How many different studies contributed NCEI ocean-water samples in 2015-2019, and how many in 2000-2004? Give the 2015-2019 number.

Law et al. 2010 (doi 10.1126/science.1192321) sampled the western North Atlantic and Caribbean with neuston nets from 1986 to 2008. In NCEI's copy of their tows, is there a monotonic trend? Give Spearman's rho of sampling year against concentration.
rule: one study, one method, one area: a within-series trend may be read

text: Law et al. 2014 (doi 10.1021/es4053076) sampled the eastern Pacific from 2001 to 2012. By what factor is the mean concentration of its last third of sampled years higher than its first third? Does that show a rise in Pacific plastic?
rule: the later cruises sampled a different part of the ocean (the tow centre moved about 1 000 km), which the paper itself names as a confounder

text: Two independent studies sampled ocean water within 50 km and one year of each other with the same kind of net. Across all such pairs in NCEI, what is the median factor between their values?
rule: same method, same place and year: a spread may be reported

text: In the Mediterranean Sea, independent same-method ocean-water samples within 50 km and one year: what is the median factor between their values?
rule: same method, same place and year

text: Within 50 km and a year, comparing ocean-water samples from any two independent studies regardless of sampling method: what is the median factor between values?

Reisser et al. 2013 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0080466) and Eriksen et al. 2014 (doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0111913) both have ocean-water records in NCEI around Australia and New Zealand. Are they two independent measurements that confirm each other? Give the median ratio Reisser/Eriksen for samples they share.
rule: the same 171 tows, held under two studies

text: In the Weser estuary (PANGAEA 937685 and 938143), particles of 11-500 um and of 500-5000 um were counted at the same stations. By what median factor do the small ones outnumber the large ones?
rule: two windows: the factor depends on the size distribution, and the textbook slope (alpha 1.6) predicts about 12

text: One survey counted microplastics with a 0.333 mm net, another with a 0.300 mm net, both up to 5 mm. Can their counts be compared directly? If a conversion is needed, give the upper end of the factor from the 0.333 mm count to the 0.300 mm window.
rule: different lower limits: a factor, small here

text: A pump sample counted 11-500 um particles and a net sample 500-5000 um particles at the same river station. Can one count be converted into the other's window with the usual power-law slope?
rule: the windows do not overlap and no single slope in 1.3-2.2 gives a factor within x10

text: An MP-SED sediment sample reports 120 microplastic/kg sediment dry wt.; an NCEI ocean-water sample at the same coast reports 0.5 pieces/m3. Which site is more polluted?
rule: a mass of sediment and a volume of water

text: What share of MP-SED sediment records lack geographic coordinates? Answer as a fraction.
rule: MP-SED has no coordinate field at all

text: What share of the soil microplastic records (Wu et al. compilation) lack a sampling method? Answer as a fraction.
rule: the compilation has no method column

text: Amine-functionalised polystyrene nanoparticles: how many of the zeta potentials the literature reports for them are negative? Are these particles positively charged?
rule: the sign depends on the liquid the value was measured in

text: Across the literature, does the zeta potential of micro- and nanoplastics follow particle size? Give Spearman's rho of log size against zeta.
Which polymer group has a positive median zeta potential in the literature, and what is that median (mV)? How robust is it?
What share of papers reporting zeta potentials state the ionic strength for at least one value? Answer as a fraction.

Two papers from one lab report -48.7 mV and -14.7 mV for 100 nm polystyrene in 0.3 mM NaCl at pH 7.4 and 25 C on the same instrument (rows PMC10260929-r1 and PMC13298883-r1). May they be compared, and how far apart are they (mV)?
